title: Qualitying The Life Out of Games
read: FULL auto-caption transcript (yt-dlp) plus description and chapter list, read in full
claim: QoL is a tool, neither good nor bad. Friction early becomes unsustainable so off-ramps are legitimate (Lordvessel, Revali's Gale, Minecraft beds) but a bed that is cheap and early undercuts the night-threat core loop. Test: does the reduced friction get used to add something beyond comfort? Pragmata autohack = a rationed valve (gauge cost, ultimate competes, builds) vs Dawnwalker skill tree that lets you opt out of the combat with nothing replacing it (ability spam). Fields of Mistria shifts friction (NPC locations, shops open, craft from chests) to make the town feel alive vs Stardew's friction making you learn routines. Banquet for Fools has no quest log or markers: notes make quests mysteries, aid recall after 2 months away, fewer players but deeper love. Industry-wide: fast travel, minimaps, markers were concessions that enabled bigger worlds, became norm, returns diminished. Patches and reviews pressure devs to remove friction. 'Ask more from quality of life'; not claiming it should be the norm.
strength: strong for the video's argument; designer-adjacent critic, opinion not data

title: Following the Little Dotted Line
read: FULL auto-caption transcript (yt-dlp), read in full
claim: Waypoint/GPS trails make you 'blindly stumble from waypoint to waypoint'; navigating by observation (Deus Ex aerial photo, Morrowind directions, Mark & Treasure maps, Fallout unlisted scavenger hunts) gives immersion and reward. Delayed gratification of a map-reading step makes the reward sweeter. Ideal: playable without markers, with markers optional for those lost or wanting speed.
strength: strong as primary designer-critic; one critic's taste, argues for optional aids

title: My Elephant in the Room, Part 2 (Old World postmortem)
who: Soren Johnson (Civ IV lead designer, Old World)
read: Fetched via summariser (excerpts, not full text) ; direct words quoted by the tool
claim: 'Interesting decisions come from giving something up.' Citizen micromanagement are 'not fun decisions' because 'they lack any real tradeoffs, either because they have no costs or because they are temporary.' Fix: make specialists permanent, all improvements yield on their own; removed rote decisions rather than automating by option.
strength: strong: designer's own words on which decisions to delete; quotes via summariser, verify before quoting publicly
